context:
Use the April 2, 2026 filtered ranking as the fixed baseline for this wave.
Sequence the work so shared fixture layers are built once and reused:
DataFrame foundation (w2) before DataFrame transaction/query work (w3-w4),
cloud-Spark mixins (w9) before Spark/LakeSail (w10-w11), and transaction
semantics (w3) before the write-primitives benchmark paths (w18).

Heavyweight adapters are intentionally isolated one module per work unit
(w7-w16, w18-w19) so each implementation step can land as a single-purpose
commit with module-local rollback.

Extend existing coverage-focused test files wherever the repo already has them.
Only add new dedicated test files when current coverage is scattered across generic
test modules and a focused file will make the missing branches easier to own.
Planned-new files are named explicitly with `Add ...`; existing files to be
extended are named explicitly with `Extend ...`.
description:

Sequencing rules for this item:
1. Harvest low-cost pure/helper wins first.
2. Build reusable DataFrame and cloud-Spark fixtures before the adapters that
   depend on them.
3. Keep heavyweight adapters isolated one per work unit when the branch
   surface is wide enough to justify dedicated review and rollback.
4. Do not spend time on results-publishing code until its productization TODO
   stabilizes the public surface.

anti_patterns.instead: assert concrete outputs, SQL fragments, state transitions, and error text instead.

anti_patterns.dont: change coverage policy to make the denominator smaller
anti_patterns.instead: close the gap with executable tests.
anti_patterns.why: that hides risk rather than reducing it

anti_patterns.dont: mix multiple heavyweight adapters into one implementation commit
anti_patterns.instead: land one work unit at a time with module-local verification.
keep those changes in the publishing stream.

anti_patterns.dont: use live cloud accounts, real Spark clusters, or real sockets to raise unit coverage
anti_patterns.instead: patch SDK clients, Spark builders, subprocesses, file I/O, and network probes.
anti_patterns.why: the fast lane must remain hermetic

deferrals.reason: Explicitly excluded from this item: `benchbox/core/publishing/**/*.py` and `benchbox/cli/commands/submit.py` are still in flight and should be planned against the publishing productization TODOs instead of this coverage wave.
Anything already excluded by `[tool.coverage.run].omit`, `[tool.coverage.report].exclude_lines`, or `pragma: no cover` is intentionally out of scope; this item targets only measured statements.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] non-actionable: Reason states coverage-ignored/omit-listed lines are intentionally out of scope by design, not deferred work needing action.

preserves.behavior: All new tests stay in the fast lane: mark them `@pytest.mark.fast` when appropriate and keep every scenario hermetic.
Assertions must verify actual SQL strings, config values, returned dataclasses, or error messages; import-only tests do not count.
Existing adapter behavior and public CLI/config contracts remain unchanged.
No new coverage ignore rules, omit entries, or `pragma: no cover` annotations are added to hit the target.
Results-publishing code stays untouched in this item.

scope_rules.path_glob: unrelated production modules outside the 25-file target set
tests/integration/** only if a named unit explicitly calls for an existing helper adjustment
tests/unit/** for the named target modules
the named production modules only when a tiny test seam is unavoidable
